NKJV.1: But King Solomon loved many foreign women, as well as the daughter of Pharaoh: women of the Moabites, Ammonites, Edomites, Sidonians, and Hittites—
NKJV.2: from the nations of whom the LORD had said to the children of Israel, “You shall not intermarry with them, nor they with you. Surely they will turn away your hearts after their gods.” Solomon clung to these in love.
NKJV.3: And he had seven hundred wives, princesses, and three hundred concubines; and his wives turned away his heart.
NKJV.4: For it was so, when Solomon was old, that his wives turned his heart after other gods; and his heart was not loyal to the LORD his God, as was the heart of his father David.
NKJV.5: For Solomon went after Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians, and after Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites.
NKJV.6: Solomon did evil in the sight of the LORD, and did not fully follow the LORD, as did his father David.
NKJV.7: Then Solomon built a high place for Chemosh the abomination of Moab, on the hill that is east of Jerusalem, and for Molech the abomination of the people of Ammon.
NKJV.8: And he did likewise for all his foreign wives, who burned incense and sacrificed to their gods.
NKJV.9: So the LORD became angry with Solomon, because his heart had turned from the LORD God of Israel, who had appeared to him twice,
NKJV.10: and had commanded him concerning this thing, that he should not go after other gods; but he did not keep what the LORD had commanded.
NKJV.11: Therefore the LORD said to Solomon, “Because you have done this, and have not kept My covenant and My statutes, which I have commanded you, I will surely tear the kingdom away from you and give it to your servant.
NKJV.12: Nevertheless I will not do it in your days, for the sake of your father David; I will tear it out of the hand of your son.
NKJV.13: However I will not tear away the whole kingdom; I will give one tribe to your son for the sake of My servant David, and for the sake of Jerusalem which I have chosen.”
NKJV.14: Now the LORD raised up an adversary against Solomon, Hadad the Edomite; he was a descendant of the king in Edom.
NKJV.15: For it happened, when David was in Edom, and Joab the commander of the army had gone up to bury the slain, after he had killed every male in Edom
NKJV.16: (because for six months Joab remained there with all Israel, until he had cut down every male in Edom),
NKJV.17: that Hadad fled to go to Egypt, he and certain Edomites of his father’s servants with him. Hadad was still a little child.
NKJV.18: Then they arose from Midian and came to Paran; and they took men with them from Paran and came to Egypt, to Pharaoh king of Egypt, who gave him a house, apportioned food for him, and gave him land.
NKJV.19: And Hadad found great favor in the sight of Pharaoh, so that he gave him as wife the sister of his own wife, that is, the sister of Queen Tahpenes.
NKJV.20: Then the sister of Tahpenes bore him Genubath his son, whom Tahpenes weaned in Pharaoh’s house. And Genubath was in Pharaoh’s household among the sons of Pharaoh.
NKJV.21: So when Hadad heard in Egypt that David rested with his fathers, and that Joab the commander of the army was dead, Hadad said to Pharaoh, “Let me depart, that I may go to my own country.”
NKJV.22: Then Pharaoh said to him, “But what have you lacked with me, that suddenly you seek to go to your own country?” So he answered, “Nothing, but do let me go anyway.”
NKJV.23: And God raised up another adversary against him, Rezon the son of Eliadah, who had fled from his lord, Hadadezer king of Zobah.
NKJV.24: So he gathered men to him and became captain over a band of raiders, when David killed those of Zobah. And they went to Damascus and dwelt there, and reigned in Damascus.
NKJV.25: He was an adversary of Israel all the days of Solomon (besides the trouble that Hadad caused); and he abhorred Israel, and reigned over Syria.
NKJV.26: Then Solomon’s servant, Jeroboam the son of Nebat, an Ephraimite from Zereda, whose mother’s name was Zeruah, a widow, also rebelled against the king.
NKJV.27: And this is what caused him to rebel against the king: Solomon had built the Millo and repaired the damages to the City of David his father.
NKJV.28: The man Jeroboam was a mighty man of valor; and Solomon, seeing that the young man was industrious, made him the officer over all the labor force of the house of Joseph.
NKJV.29: Now it happened at that time, when Jeroboam went out of Jerusalem, that the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite met him on the way; and he had clothed himself with a new garment, and the two were alone in the field.
NKJV.30: Then Ahijah took hold of the new garment that was on him, and tore it into twelve pieces.
NKJV.31: And he said to Jeroboam, “Take for yourself ten pieces, for thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: ‘Behold, I will tear the kingdom out of the hand of Solomon and will give ten tribes to you
NKJV.32: (but he shall have one tribe for the sake of My servant David, and for the sake of Jerusalem, the city which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel),
NKJV.33: because they have forsaken Me, and worshiped Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians, Chemosh the god of the Moabites, and Milcom the god of the people of Ammon, and have not walked in My ways to do what is right in My eyes and keep My statutes and My judgments, as did his father David.
NKJV.34: However I will not take the whole kingdom out of his hand, because I have made him ruler all the days of his life for the sake of My servant David, whom I chose because he kept My commandments and My statutes.
NKJV.35: But I will take the kingdom out of his son’s hand and give it to you—ten tribes.
NKJV.36: And to his son I will give one tribe, that My servant David may always have a lamp before Me in Jerusalem, the city which I have chosen for Myself, to put My name there.
NKJV.37: So I will take you, and you shall reign over all your heart desires, and you shall be king over Israel.
NKJV.38: Then it shall be, if you heed all that I command you, walk in My ways, and do what is right in My sight, to keep My statutes and My commandments, as My servant David did, then I will be with you and build for you an enduring house, as I built for David, and will give Israel to you.
NKJV.39: And I will afflict the descendants of David because of this, but not forever.’ ”
NKJV.40: Solomon therefore sought to kill Jeroboam. But Jeroboam arose and fled to Egypt, to Shishak king of Egypt, and was in Egypt until the death of Solomon.
NKJV.41: Now the rest of the acts of Solomon, all that he did, and his wisdom, are they not written in the book of the acts of Solomon?
NKJV.42: And the period that Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel was forty years.
NKJV.43: Then Solomon rested with his fathers, and was buried in the City of David his father. And Rehoboam his son reigned in his place.

NLT.1: Now King Solomon loved many foreign women. Besides Pharaoh’s daughter, he married women from Moab, Ammon, Edom, Sidon, and from among the Hittites.
NLT.2: The LORD had clearly instructed the people of Israel, “You must not marry them, because they will turn your hearts to their gods.” Yet Solomon insisted on loving them anyway.
NLT.3: He had 700 wives of royal birth and 300 concubines. And in fact, they did turn his heart away from the LORD.
NLT.4: In Solomon’s old age, they turned his heart to worship other gods instead of being completely faithful to the LORD his God, as his father, David, had been.
NLT.5: Solomon worshiped Ashtoreth, the goddess of the Sidonians, and Molech, the detestable god of the Ammonites.
NLT.6: In this way, Solomon did what was evil in the LORD’s sight; he refused to follow the LORD completely, as his father, David, had done.
NLT.7: On the Mount of Olives, east of Jerusalem, he even built a pagan shrine for Chemosh, the detestable god of Moab, and another for Molech, the detestable god of the Ammonites.
NLT.8: Solomon built such shrines for all his foreign wives to use for burning incense and sacrificing to their gods.
NLT.9: The LORD was very angry with Solomon, for his heart had turned away from the LORD, the God of Israel, who had appeared to him twice.
NLT.10: He had warned Solomon specifically about worshiping other gods, but Solomon did not listen to the LORD’s command.
NLT.11: So now the LORD said to him, “Since you have not kept my covenant and have disobeyed my decrees, I will surely tear the kingdom away from you and give it to one of your servants.
NLT.12: But for the sake of your father, David, I will not do this while you are still alive. I will take the kingdom away from your son.
NLT.13: And even so, I will not take away the entire kingdom; I will let him be king of one tribe, for the sake of my servant David and for the sake of Jerusalem, my chosen city.”
NLT.14: Then the LORD raised up Hadad the Edomite, a member of Edom’s royal family, to be Solomon’s adversary.
NLT.15: Years before, David had defeated Edom. Joab, his army commander, had stayed to bury some of the Israelite soldiers who had died in battle. While there, they killed every male in Edom.
NLT.16: Joab and the army of Israel had stayed there for six months, killing them.
NLT.17: But Hadad and a few of his father’s royal officials escaped and headed for Egypt. (Hadad was just a boy at the time.)
NLT.18: They set out from Midian and went to Paran, where others joined them. Then they traveled to Egypt and went to Pharaoh, who gave them a home, food, and some land.
NLT.19: Pharaoh grew very fond of Hadad, and he gave him his wife’s sister in marriage — the sister of Queen Tahpenes.
NLT.20: She bore him a son named Genubath. Tahpenes raised him in Pharaoh’s palace among Pharaoh’s own sons.
NLT.21: When the news reached Hadad in Egypt that David and his commander Joab were both dead, he said to Pharaoh, “Let me return to my own country.”
NLT.22: “Why?” Pharaoh asked him. “What do you lack here that makes you want to go home?” “Nothing,” he replied. “But even so, please let me return home.”
NLT.23: God also raised up Rezon son of Eliada as Solomon’s adversary. Rezon had fled from his master, King Hadadezer of Zobah,
NLT.24: and had become the leader of a gang of rebels. After David conquered Hadadezer, Rezon and his men fled to Damascus, where he became king.
NLT.25: Rezon was Israel’s bitter adversary for the rest of Solomon’s reign, and he made trouble, just as Hadad did. Rezon hated Israel intensely and continued to reign in Aram.
NLT.26: Another rebel leader was Jeroboam son of Nebat, one of Solomon’s own officials. He came from the town of Zeredah in Ephraim, and his mother was Zeruah, a widow.
NLT.27: This is the story behind his rebellion. Solomon was rebuilding the supporting terraces and repairing the walls of the city of his father, David.
NLT.28: Jeroboam was a very capable young man, and when Solomon saw how industrious he was, he put him in charge of the labor force from the tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh, the descendants of Joseph.
NLT.29: One day as Jeroboam was leaving Jerusalem, the prophet Ahijah from Shiloh met him along the way. Ahijah was wearing a new cloak. The two of them were alone in a field,
NLT.30: and Ahijah took hold of the new cloak he was wearing and tore it into twelve pieces.
NLT.31: Then he said to Jeroboam, “Take ten of these pieces, for this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘I am about to tear the kingdom from the hand of Solomon, and I will give ten of the tribes to you!
NLT.32: But I will leave him one tribe for the sake of my servant David and for the sake of Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel.
NLT.33: For Solomon has abandoned me and worshiped Ashtoreth, the goddess of the Sidonians; Chemosh, the god of Moab; and Molech, the god of the Ammonites. He has not followed my ways and done what is pleasing in my sight. He has not obeyed my decrees and regulations as David his father did.
NLT.34: “‘But I will not take the entire kingdom from Solomon at this time. For the sake of my servant David, the one whom I chose and who obeyed my commands and decrees, I will keep Solomon as leader for the rest of his life.
NLT.35: But I will take the kingdom away from his son and give ten of the tribes to you.
NLT.36: His son will have one tribe so that the descendants of David my servant will continue to reign, shining like a lamp in Jerusalem, the city I have chosen to be the place for my name.
NLT.37: And I will place you on the throne of Israel, and you will rule over all that your heart desires.
NLT.38: If you listen to what I tell you and follow my ways and do whatever I consider to be right, and if you obey my decrees and commands, as my servant David did, then I will always be with you. I will establish an enduring dynasty for you as I did for David, and I will give Israel to you.
NLT.39: Because of Solomon’s sin I will punish the descendants of David — though not forever.’”
NLT.40: Solomon tried to kill Jeroboam, but he fled to King Shishak of Egypt and stayed there until Solomon died.
NLT.41: The rest of the events in Solomon’s reign, including all his deeds and his wisdom, are recorded in The Book of the Acts of Solomon.
NLT.42: Solomon ruled in Jerusalem over all Israel for forty years.
NLT.43: When he died, he was buried in the City of David, named for his father. Then his son Rehoboam became the next king.

CSB17.1: King Solomon loved many foreign women in addition to Pharaoh’s daughter: <sup>ⓖ</sup> Moabite, Ammonite, Edomite, Sidonian, and Hittite women <sup>ⓗ</sup>
CSB17.2: from the nations about which the LORD had told the Israelites, “You must not intermarry with them, and they must not intermarry with you, because they will turn your heart away to follow their gods.” <sup>ⓘ</sup> To these women Solomon was deeply attached <sup>[1]</sup> in love.
CSB17.3: He had seven hundred wives who were princesses and three hundred who were concubines, <sup>ⓙ</sup> and they turned his heart away. <sup>ⓚ</sup>
CSB17.4: When Solomon was old, his wives turned his heart away to follow other gods. He was not wholeheartedly devoted to the LORD his God, as his father David had been. <sup>ⓛ</sup>
CSB17.5: Solomon followed Ashtoreth, <sup>ⓜ</sup> the goddess of the Sidonians, and Milcom, <sup>ⓝ</sup> the abhorrent idol of the Ammonites. <sup>ⓐ</sup>
CSB17.6: Solomon did what was evil in the LORD’s sight, and unlike his father David, he did not remain loyal to the LORD.
CSB17.7: At that time, Solomon built a high place <sup>ⓑ</sup> for Chemosh, <sup>ⓒ</sup> the abhorrent idol of Moab, and for Milcom, <sup>[2]</sup> <sup>ⓓ</sup> the abhorrent idol of the Ammonites, on the hill across from Jerusalem. <sup>ⓔ</sup>
CSB17.8: He did the same for all his foreign wives, who were burning incense and offering sacrifices to their gods.
CSB17.9: The LORD was angry with Solomon, because his heart had turned away from the LORD, the God of Israel, who had appeared to him twice. <sup>ⓕ</sup>
CSB17.10: He had commanded him about this, so that he would not follow other gods, but Solomon did not do what the LORD had commanded. <sup>ⓖ</sup>
CSB17.11: Then the LORD said to Solomon, “Since you have done this <sup>[3]</sup> and did not keep my covenant and my statutes, which I commanded you, I will tear the kingdom away from you and give it to your servant. <sup>ⓗ</sup>
CSB17.12: However, I will not do it during your lifetime for the sake of your father David; <sup>ⓘ</sup> I will tear it out of your son’s hand.
CSB17.13: Yet I will not tear the entire kingdom away from him. I will give one tribe to your son <sup>ⓙ</sup> for the sake of my servant David and for the sake of Jerusalem that I chose.”
CSB17.14: So the LORD raised up <sup>ⓚ</sup> Hadad the Edomite as an enemy against Solomon. He was of the royal family in Edom.
CSB17.15: Earlier, when David was in Edom, Joab, the commander of the army, had gone to bury the dead and had struck down every male in Edom.
CSB17.16: For Joab and all Israel had remained there six months, until he had killed every male in Edom. <sup>ⓛ</sup>
CSB17.17: Hadad fled to Egypt, along with some Edomites from his father’s servants. At the time Hadad was a small boy.
CSB17.18: Hadad and his men set out from Midian and went to Paran. <sup>ⓜ</sup> They took men with them from Paran and went to Egypt, to Pharaoh king of Egypt, <sup>ⓝ</sup> who gave Hadad a house, ordered that he be given food, and gave him land.
CSB17.19: Pharaoh liked Hadad so much <sup>[4]</sup> that he gave him a wife, the sister of his own wife, Queen Tahpenes.
CSB17.20: Tahpenes’s sister gave birth to Hadad’s son Genubath. Tahpenes herself weaned him in Pharaoh’s palace, and Genubath lived there along with Pharaoh’s sons.
CSB17.21: When Hadad heard in Egypt that David rested with his fathers and that Joab, the commander of the army, was dead, Hadad said to Pharaoh, “Let me leave, so I may go to my own country.”
CSB17.22: But Pharaoh asked him, “What do you lack here with me for you to want to go back to your own country?” “Nothing,” he replied, “but please let me leave.”
CSB17.23: God raised up Rezon son of Eliada as an enemy <sup>ⓐ</sup> against Solomon. Rezon had fled from his master King Hadadezer of Zobah <sup>ⓑ</sup>
CSB17.24: and gathered men to himself. He became leader of a raiding party when David killed the Zobaites. He <sup>[5]</sup> went to Damascus, <sup>ⓒ</sup> lived there, and became king in Damascus.
CSB17.25: Rezon was Israel’s enemy throughout Solomon’s reign, adding to the trouble Hadad had caused. He reigned over Aram <sup>[6]</sup> <sup>ⓓ</sup> and loathed Israel.
CSB17.26: Now Solomon’s servant, <sup>ⓔ</sup> Jeroboam son of Nebat, was an Ephraimite from Zeredah. His widowed mother’s name was Zeruah. Jeroboam rebelled <sup>ⓕ</sup> against Solomon,
CSB17.27: and this is the reason he rebelled against the king: Solomon had built the supporting terraces <sup>ⓖ</sup> and repaired the opening in the wall of the city of his father David.
CSB17.28: Now the man Jeroboam was capable, and Solomon noticed the young man because he was getting things done. So he appointed him over the entire labor force of the house of Joseph. <sup>ⓗ</sup>
CSB17.29: During that time, the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite <sup>ⓘ</sup> met Jeroboam on the road as Jeroboam came out of Jerusalem. Now Ahijah had wrapped himself with a new cloak, and the two of them were alone in the open field.
CSB17.30: Then Ahijah took hold of the new cloak he had on, tore it into twelve pieces, <sup>ⓙ</sup>
CSB17.31: and said to Jeroboam, “Take ten pieces for yourself, for this is what the LORD God of Israel says: ‘I am about to tear the kingdom out of Solomon’s hand. I will give you ten tribes,
CSB17.32: but one tribe will remain his for the sake of my servant David <sup>ⓚ</sup> and for the sake of Jerusalem, the city I chose out of all the tribes of Israel. <sup>ⓛ</sup>
CSB17.33: For they have abandoned me; they have bowed down to Ashtoreth, the goddess of the Sidonians, to Chemosh, the god of Moab, and to Milcom, the god of the Ammonites. <sup>ⓜ</sup> They have not walked in my ways to do what is right in my sight and to carry out my statutes and my judgments as his father David did. <sup>ⓝ</sup>
CSB17.34: “‘However, I will not take the whole kingdom from him but will let him be ruler all the days of his life for the sake of my servant David, whom I chose and who kept my commands and my statutes.
CSB17.35: I will take ten tribes of the kingdom from his son and give them to you.
CSB17.36: I will give one tribe <sup>ⓐ</sup> to his son, <sup>ⓑ</sup> so that my servant David will always have a lamp before me <sup>ⓒ</sup> in Jerusalem, the city I chose for myself to put my name there. <sup>ⓓ</sup>
CSB17.37: I will appoint you, <sup>ⓔ</sup> and you will reign as king <sup>ⓕ</sup> over all you want, <sup>ⓖ</sup> and you will be king over Israel.
CSB17.38: “‘After that, if you obey all I command you, walk in my ways, and do what is right in my sight in order to keep my statutes and my commands as my servant David did, I will be with you. <sup>ⓗ</sup> I will build you a lasting dynasty just as I built for David, <sup>ⓘ</sup> and I will give you Israel.
CSB17.39: I will humble David’s descendants, because of their unfaithfulness, but not forever.’” <sup>[7]</sup> <sup>ⓙ</sup>
CSB17.40: Therefore, Solomon tried to kill Jeroboam, <sup>ⓚ</sup> but he fled to Egypt, <sup>ⓛ</sup> to King Shishak of Egypt, <sup>ⓜ</sup> where he remained until Solomon’s death.
CSB17.41: The rest of the events of Solomon’s reign, along with all his accomplishments and his wisdom, are written in the Book of Solomon’s Events. <sup>ⓝ</sup>
CSB17.42: The length of Solomon’s reign in Jerusalem over all Israel totaled forty years. <sup>ⓐ</sup>
CSB17.43: Solomon rested with his fathers and was buried in the city of his father David. His son Rehoboam <sup>ⓑ</sup> became king in his place. <sup>ⓒ</sup>

MSG.19: Pharaoh liked him so well that he gave him the sister of his wife, Queen Tahpenes, in marriage.
MSG.20: She bore Hadad a son named Genubath who was raised like one of the royal family. Genubath grew up in the palace with Pharaoh's children.
MSG.21: While living in Egypt, Hadad heard that both David and Joab, commander of the army, were dead. He approached Pharaoh and said, "Send me off with your blessing—I want to return to my country."
MSG.22:
"But why?" said Pharaoh. "Why would you want to leave here? Hasn't everything been to your liking?"
"Everything has been just fine," said Hadad, "but I want to go home—give me a good send-off!"
MSG.23: Then God incited another adversary against Solomon, Rezon son of Eliada, who had deserted from his master, Hadadezer king of Zobah.
MSG.24: After David's slaughter of the Arameans, Rezon collected a band of outlaws and became their leader. They later settled in Damascus, where Rezon eventually took over as king.
MSG.25: Like Hadad, Rezon was a thorn in Israel's side all of Solomon's life. He was king over Aram, and he hated Israel.
MSG.26: And then, the last straw: Jeroboam son of Nebat rebelled against the king. He was an Ephraimite from Zeredah, his mother a widow named Zeruah. He served in Solomon's administration.
MSG.27: This is why he rebelled. Solomon had built the outer defense system (the Millo) and had restored the fortifications that were in disrepair from the time of his father David.
MSG.28: Jeroboam stood out during the construction as strong and able. When Solomon observed what a good worker he was, he put the young man in charge of the entire workforce of the tribe of Joseph.
MSG.29: One day Jeroboam was walking down the road out of Jerusalem. Ahijah the prophet of Shiloh, wearing a brand-new cloak, met him. The two of them were alone on that remote stretch of road.
MSG.30: Ahijah took off the new cloak that he was wearing and ripped it into twelve pieces.
MSG.31: Then he said to Jeroboam, "Take ten of these pieces for yourself; this is by order of the God of Israel: See what I'm doing—I'm ripping the kingdom out of Solomon's hands and giving you ten of the tribes.
MSG.32: In honor of my servant David and out of respect for Jerusalem, the city I especially chose, he will get one tribe.
MSG.33: And here's the reason: He faithlessly abandoned me and went off worshiping Ashtoreth goddess of the Sidonians, Chemosh god of the Moabites, and Molech god of the Ammonites. He hasn't lived the way I have shown him, hasn't done what I have wanted, and hasn't followed directions or obeyed orders as his father David did.
MSG.34: "Still, I won't take the whole kingdom away from him. I'll stick with him through his lifetime because of my servant David whom I chose and who did follow my directions and obey my orders.
MSG.35: But after that I'll remove the kingdom from his son's control and give you ten tribes.
MSG.36: I'll leave one tribe to his son, to maintain a witness to my servant David in Jerusalem, the city I chose as a memorial to my Name.
MSG.37: "But I have taken you in hand. Rule to your heart's content! You are to be the king of Israel.
MSG.38: If you listen to what I tell you and live the way I show you and do what pleases me, following directions and obeying orders as my servant David did, I'll stick with you no matter what. I'll build you a kingdom as solid as the one I built for David. Israel will be yours!
MSG.39: I am bringing pain and trouble on David's descendants, but the trials won't last forever."
MSG.40: Solomon ordered the assassination of Jeroboam, but he got away to Egypt and found asylum there with King Shishak. He remained in exile there until Solomon died.
MSG.41: The rest of Solomon's life and rule, his work and his wisdom, you can read for yourself in The Chronicles of Solomon.
MSG.42: Solomon ruled in Jerusalem over all Israel for forty years.
MSG.43: He died and was buried in the City of David his father. His son Rehoboam was the next king.

NET.1: King Solomon fell in love with many foreign women (besides Pharaoh’s daughter), including Moabites, Ammonites, Edomites, Sidonians, and Hittites.
NET.2: They came from nations about which the LORD had warned the Israelites, “You must not establish friendly relations with them! If you do, they will surely shift your allegiance to their gods.” But Solomon was irresistibly attracted to them.
NET.3: He had 700 royal wives and 300 concubines; his wives had a powerful influence over him.
NET.4: When Solomon became old, his wives shifted his allegiance to other gods; he was not wholeheartedly devoted to the LORD his God, as his father David had been.
NET.5: Solomon worshiped the Sidonian goddess Astarte and the detestable Ammonite god Milcom.
NET.6: Solomon did evil in the LORD’s sight; he did not remain loyal to the LORD, like his father David had.
NET.7: Furthermore, on the hill east of Jerusalem Solomon built a high place for the detestable Moabite god Chemosh and for the detestable Ammonite god Milcom.
NET.8: He built high places for all his foreign wives so they could burn incense and make sacrifices to their gods.
NET.9: The LORD was angry with Solomon because he had shifted his allegiance away from the LORD, the God of Israel, who had appeared to him on two occasions
NET.10: and had warned him about this very thing, so that he would not follow other gods. But he did not obey the LORD’s command.
NET.11: So the LORD said to Solomon, “Because you insist on doing these things and have not kept the covenantal rules I gave you, I will surely tear the kingdom away from you and give it to your servant.
NET.12: However, for your father David’s sake I will not do this while you are alive. I will tear it away from your son’s hand instead.
NET.13: But I will not tear away the entire kingdom; I will leave your son one tribe for my servant David’s sake and for the sake of my chosen city Jerusalem.”
NET.14: The LORD brought against Solomon an enemy, Hadad the Edomite, a descendant of the Edomite king.
NET.15: During David’s campaign against Edom, Joab, the commander of the army, while on a mission to bury the dead, killed every male in Edom.
NET.16: For six months Joab and the entire Israelite army stayed there until they had exterminated every male in Edom.
NET.17: Hadad, who was only a small boy at the time, escaped with some of his father’s Edomite servants and headed for Egypt.
NET.18: They went from Midian to Paran; they took some men from Paran and went to Egypt. Pharaoh, king of Egypt, supplied him with a house and food and even assigned him some land.
NET.19: Pharaoh liked Hadad so well he gave him his sister-in-law (Queen Tahpenes’ sister) as a wife.
NET.20: Tahpenes’ sister gave birth to his son, named Genubath. Tahpenes raised him in Pharaoh’s palace; Genubath grew up in Pharaoh’s palace among Pharaoh’s sons.
NET.21: While in Egypt Hadad heard that David had passed away and that Joab, the commander of the army, was dead. So Hadad asked Pharaoh, “Give me permission to leave so I can return to my homeland.”
NET.22: Pharaoh said to him, “What do you lack here that makes you want to go to your homeland?” Hadad replied, “Nothing, but please give me permission to leave.”
NET.23: God also brought against Solomon another enemy, Rezon son of Eliada who had run away from his master, King Hadadezer of Zobah.
NET.24: He gathered some men and organized a raiding band. When David tried to kill them, they went to Damascus, where they settled down and gained control of the city.
NET.25: He was Israel’s enemy throughout Solomon’s reign and, like Hadad, caused trouble. He loathed Israel and ruled over Syria.
NET.26: Jeroboam son of Nebat, one of Solomon’s servants, rebelled against the king. He was an Ephraimite from Zeredah whose mother was a widow named Zeruah.
NET.27: This is what prompted him to rebel against the king: Solomon built a terrace and he closed up a gap in the wall of the city of his father David.
NET.28: Jeroboam was a talented man; when Solomon saw that the young man was an accomplished worker, he made him the leader of the work crew from the tribe of Joseph.
NET.29: At that time, when Jeroboam had left Jerusalem, the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite met him on the road; the two of them were alone in the open country. Ahijah was wearing a brand new robe,
NET.30: and he grabbed the robe and tore it into twelve pieces.
NET.31: Then he told Jeroboam, “Take ten pieces, for this is what the LORD God of Israel says: ‘Look, I am about to tear the kingdom from Solomon’s hand and I will give ten tribes to you.
NET.32: He will retain one tribe, for my servant David’s sake and for the sake of Jerusalem, the city I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel.
NET.33: I am taking the kingdom from him because they have abandoned me and worshiped the Sidonian goddess Astarte, the Moabite god Chemosh, and the Ammonite god Milcom. They have not followed my instructions by doing what I approve and obeying my rules and regulations, like Solomon’s father David did.
NET.34: I will not take the whole kingdom from his hand. I will allow him to be ruler for the rest of his life for the sake of my chosen servant David who kept my commandments and rules.
NET.35: I will take the kingdom from the hand of his son and give ten tribes to you.
NET.36: I will leave his son one tribe so my servant David’s dynasty may continue to serve me in Jerusalem, the city I have chosen as my home.
NET.37: I will select you; you will rule over all you desire to have and you will be king over Israel.
NET.38: You must obey all I command you to do, follow my instructions, do what I approve, and keep my rules and commandments, like my servant David did. Then I will be with you and establish for you a lasting dynasty, as I did for David; I will give you Israel.
NET.39: I will humiliate David’s descendants because of this, but not forever.”
NET.40: Solomon tried to kill Jeroboam, but Jeroboam escaped to Egypt and found refuge with King Shishak of Egypt. He stayed in Egypt until Solomon died.
NET.41: The rest of the events of Solomon’s reign, including all his accomplishments and his wise decisions, are recorded in the scroll called the Annals of Solomon.
NET.42: Solomon ruled over all Israel from Jerusalem for forty years.
NET.43: Then Solomon passed away and was buried in the city of his father David. His son Rehoboam replaced him as king.
